newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO View-China's First Tractor seen drawing intere.
newsitem.headline: IPO View-China's First Tractor seen drawing intere.

text.p: First Tractor Co Ltd is expected to become the latest China-linked company to draw strong investor interest with a planned Hong Kong listing, analysts said.
Investors see First Tractor, China's largest manufacturer of agricultural tractors, as a major beneficiary of Beijing's programme to promote agricultural development, analysts said.

The H-share company should also benefit from limited foreign competition, although analysts say over time China will be forced to allow the entry of foreign firms to comply with international standards of free trade.
"It is likely to be another popular issue following Beijing Enterprises ahead of the handover," said Ben Kwong, director of research of Dharmala Securities.
"It is attractive because of its agricultural concept."

Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd, a red-chip backed by the Beijing municipal government, drew record subscription levels ahead of its debut on May 29. The share price closed on Friday at HK$50.25, more than four times its issue price.
Red chips are Hong Kong-incorporated companies with mainland Chinese financial backing. H-shares are Hong Kong-listed shares of China-incorporated enterprises.

First Tractor is the largest manufacturer of agricultural tractors in China in terms of turnover and production volume, accounting for about 16 percent of total turnover of the industry in 1996, analysts said.
"It appears to be the hottest among other upcoming H-shares ahead of the Hong Kong handover," said Kelvin Tang, analyst at Impac Asset Management (HK) Ltd.

Tang said there was strong demand from investors "who want to tap the growth in China's agricultural sector, particularly after China has emphasised its intention to develop agriculture in coming years."
An analyst at DBS Securities said there was strong domestic demand for the company's products and "little market competition given the market is not yet open to foreign competitors."
First Tractor is expected to issue 300 million H-shares or 40 percent of its enlarged share capital in a global flotation.
Of the total, 255 million shares will be earmarked for international placement, and 45 million shares will be offered to Hong Kong investors by public offering, analysts said.
Market sources said the portion for international placement was likely to be more than 20 times subscribed.
In view of the expected strong response, the company raised the issue price to between a range of HK$3.95 to HK$4.50 per share from the previous HK$3.12 to HK$3.97, sources said.

The new issue price will represent a prospective price to earnings (P/E) multiple of between 11.79 and 13 times on a fully-diluted basis, and from 10.21 to 11.5 times on a weighted average basis, the sources said.
The initial issue price represented a prospective P/E of 9.45 to 11.84 times on a fully-diluted basis and 8.10 to 10.31 times on a weighted average basis.
"In view of the P/E of other H-share candidates, First Tractor is not that expensive (after the revision)," said Rachael Tsang, analyst at Vickers Ballas Securities.
Tang, of Impac Asset Management, said the company had reached its peak of capacity but intends to expand.
"Its business prospects and growth potential are seen as huge following its expansion of production capability," he said.
First Tractor is expected to use the proceeds to expand manufacturing capacity, reduce debt, and as working capital.
The Hong Kong public offering will run from June 11 to 16 and dealing in the shares is expected to begin on June 23.
Analysts said investors seeking to diversify among H shares also might prefer First Tractor as the first agricultural listing.
